Component_Tested: Week 6 finding: "HF013, HF014, HF010 are busiest; HF019 quietest"
Scenario: Hospital volumes differ more than chance would explain (chi-square, p < 0.05)
Actual_Result: chi-square p = 0.052, borderline (range 217 to 278 against 250 expected)
Issue_Identified: Differences in hospital volume are not reliable at the 5% level (borderline) and are close to random variation
Action_Taken: Re-worded: hospitals are described as "similar in volume"; ranking by volume kept only as a descriptive table
Retest_Result: Recommendation 1 (move doctors) changed from "re-balance now" to "monitor monthly"

Component_Tested: Week 6 finding: "same staff, uneven workload: 12.3 to 16.4 appointments per doctor"
Scenario: Doctor numbers (17 or 18 per hospital) explain most of the spread
Expected_Result: Spread of about 13.9 to 14.7 if volume were equal
Actual_Result: Observed 12.3 to 16.4; the extra spread comes from appointment volume, which test F01 shows is not reliably different
Issue_Identified: The "uneven allocation" finding is not supported as stated: staffing is nearly flat (17 or 18 doctors, 35 nurses everywhere) and volume differences are chance
Action_Taken: Replaced by a fact that is supported: staffing does not vary with demand because every hospital has the same team size; the 12-to-16 range is shown as descriptive only
Retest_Result: Reworded finding verified: nurses per hospital all 35; doctors 17 or 18

Component_Tested: Week 6 finding: "busiest hospitals are among the least liked" (HF013, HF014 rated 2.77)
Scenario: Hospital ratings differ by more than chance (ANOVA p < 0.05)

Action_Taken: Removed the claim from the key messages; hospital ratings now shown with sample size and 95% confidence range (see section 8)

Actual_Result: range 12.3 to 16.4 per doctor; chi-square p = 0.010
Action_Taken: Kept as a supported but modest finding: workload per doctor varies by more than chance, although hospital volume alone is borderline (F01, p = 0.052)
Retest_Result: Recommendation 1 stays "monitor monthly and re-test with the full appointment list" (see decision DL-08)

Component_Tested: Claims approval (cross-track test with Project Management)
Scenario: Claim approval differs by insurer, payment method, claim amount or visit type (chi-square p < 0.05)
Expected_Result: p < 0.05 if approval depends on the field
Actual_Result: approved 50.0% overall; insurer 49.3% to 50.9% (p = 0.077); payment method 49.4% to 50.9% (p = 0.17); amount quartile 49.7% to 50.4% (p = 0.74); visit type 49.0% to 51.4%
Issue_Identified: No evidence that approval depends on any available field, so a claims model has no signal to learn from these fields
Action_Taken: Result sent to the Project Manager to compare with the claims model result (accuracy 50.1%)
Retest_Result: Reply received 2 Nov 2026, 12:10 AM: the Project Manager thanked me and said she had submitted. She did not report a changed model result, target or label, so no numerical retest was possible; the test and finding stand as sent
